title: The League of Kitchens: Cooking Classes in NYC

services.name: Private Events
services.desc: Make your next gathering unforgettable. Whether you’re hosting a company holiday party, team-building event, client dinner, birthday celebration, or reunion, the League of Kitchens transforms every occasion into something meaningful and delicious. The League of Kitchens is a New York City-based cooking school and private events company offering hands-on, multicultural cooking experiences led by immigrant women from around the world. Our instructors-extraordinary home cooks representing 13 countries-welcome you into their kitchens to share their tips, traditions, and stories. We design private cooking events in NYC and online that are filled with love and laughter. Each event is much more

services.name: Upcoming Cooking Classes
services.desc: Online: All Online cooking classes are live online classes where participants cook in their own kitchens during the class. They include interactive cooking instruction, a virtual dinner party, a packet with the instructor's family recipes, and a video recording of the class. Immersion: All Immersion workshops take place in the instructor's home and include a light lunch and beverage, 3 hours of hands-on cooking instruction, a full dinner, a recipe packet, and a shopping guide. Taste Of: All Taste Of workshops include a welcome snack and beverage, 1.5 hours of hands-on cooking instruction, a small meal, a recipe packet, and a shopping guide. Don't see a class that fits your schedule? Join

quotes.author: Mark Bittman, The Bittman Project
quotes.text: A cookbook I’ve been waiting years for—recipes by immigrants to America from all over the world. The breadth, the authenticity, the emotion, the beauty, the flavors, the challenges—unsurpassed.

quotes.author: Monique Z.
quotes.text: I wanted a team activity where my colleagues could come together and learn about other cultures while sharing a bit about themselves over a meal. It was perfect. Jeanette overwhelmed us with her warmth, kindness, and humor. Her food was delicious and plentiful. I love the whole concept of the League of Kitchens and will certainly recommend it to others.

quotes.author: Miguel M.
quotes.text: To say we had a wonderful experience would be an understatement. With great storytelling, delicious food, kind hospitality and overall camaraderie; this was a highlight of our NYC experience! If we could give Shandra and League of Kitchens more than five stars, we definitely would!

quotes.author: Jordan J.
quotes.text: Our experience with the group was fantastic! The whole team went above and beyond to make our offsite so special for the team. From prepping to clean-up, this team was amazing!

quotes.author: Evan Kleinman, KCRW's Good Food
quotes.text: Every page of this book has a story I want to hear and a dish I want to make
The perfect class for New Yorkers or tourists. The food was amazing, easy to prepare and I've infused the lesson with all my cooking...” more

I was part of a small group welcomed into Afsari's kitchen for an hours-long cooking class, learning to make some delicious Bangladeshi cuisine, including Palak Paneer, an eggplant dish, flat bread, and probably the best rice pudding I've ever tasted...” more

A collection of culinary wisdom from women all over the world, this beautiful book details the subtle techniques passed down for generations that turn an ordinary meal into a magical one. I will be making every single recipe!

I've been fortunate enough to take several League of Kitchen classes, and nothing beats learning to cook a new-to-you cuisine in someone's home kitchen. But the recipes and photos in the League of Kitchen's stunning cookbook make you feel like you are standing at the stovetop with a spoon in your hand and the teacher by your side. It is truly the next best thing.

The recipes represent a wide range of cuisines, including Afghan, Lebanese, Mexican, Bangladeshi, Greek, Indonesian, Japanese, and more. There are also spotlights on the different instructors who shared their recipes for the book. I was particularly excited to see the profile of and recipes from Damira Inatullaeva, whose Uzbek cooking class I enjoyed immensely last year.

The whole day was relaxed and lovely. Afsari was welcoming and taught us so much about her own life and about the food. I truly had so much fun and learned a ton. The experience far exceeded my expectations. I was thrilled with how many leftovers we were able to take home. The value was increased by the fact that I get to continue eating this lovely meal for lunch for two days!

I felt extraordinarily comfortable in Rachana’s home. It was a privilege and honor to be welcomed so openly and generously, plus I learned A LOT about Nepali food and ingredients and about Rachana’s family and unique cultural perspective. Everything she shared was very interesting. And I definitely think I can replicate a lot of these dishes at home, which is not what I expected. But they aren’t nearly so intimidating now!
